text:
anya: Quick sync — I ran the onboarding eval for petal-v2 (base float32 -> int8) on the wiki+search holdout. Seeing a weird R@1 regression.
anya: float32 R@1=0.82, int8 (default per-tensor) R@1=0.76, R@10 almost same (0.93 -> 0.92).
anya: UMAP shows cluster centroids shifted for several topical cohorts, silhouette down ~0.04. images: https://redwood.internal/embeds/petal-v2/umap_shift.png
mike: ouch. dims? pooling?
anya: 768-dim, mean pooling, no extra whitening. identical preprocessing.
sanjay: did you use per-channel qparams or per-tensor? per-channel usually helps preserve relative scales.
anya: ran default converter -> per-tensor int8. didn't try per-channel yet.
tara: also check whether layernorm folding happened in the ONNX path — that can cause small mean shifts that kill R@1.
leo: re-ran local repro with `python eval_embeddings.py --model petal-v2 --quant int8 --holdout wiki_search --k 1,10` got:
```
# eval output snippet
R@1: 0.7604
R@10: 0.9258
mean_cos_shift: -0.0117
silhouette: 0.312 -> 0.274
```
leo: posted the full run at https://redwood.internal/runs/1766667777 (artifacts + per-cohort csv)
sanjay: try int8 per-channel and per-channel asymmetric — also check scale clamp. can you diff centroid norms?
anya: quick diff: mean L2 centroid norm (float32)=1.02, (int8)=0.985, so ~3.5% shrink.
mike: interesting — that could explain nearest-neighbor flips. try rescaling post-quant by the centroid norm ratio as a diagnostic.
tara: also run the same eval but with a 32-bit calibration table (fake quant) — to see if calibration data is the issue. sometimes the calibration samples bias low-frequency tokens / heads.
leo: I can run per-channel int8 + alternate calibrations by EOD. want me to also run a small A/B on the production recall route?
anya: yes please. also add a quick kNN confusion matrix for the top 5 neighbours so we can see which classes flip.
eval-bot: Job 1766667777-umbra-eval completed — artifacts uploaded (embeddings.csv, recall_k.csv, cohort_umap.png).
sanjay: if per-channel fixes it, we should update our quant recommendation for 768-dim models to prefer per-channel for petal family.
mike: agreed. but if not, we need to check serving pipeline (normalization, cache warmup). sometimes KV cache tokenization mismatch shows up as small shifts.
tara: next steps: 1) leo run per-channel + 2 calibration sets, 2) anya produce kNN flip table and per-cohort recall, 3) run quick canary (small slice) on prod route. assign leo/anya.
anya: ack. will also add the UMAP overlays comparing float32/int8 for the top 10 cohorts.
leo: starting; ping here when results ready. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
mike: thanks — keeping this thread as the single place for artifacts. if we see persistent R@1 drops >0.03 we'll hold rollout. :warning:
